2	title: Follow the speaker in a vertical
3	description: Make a vertical version of a wide interview that cuts to whoever is talking, using a microphone per person.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A wide shot of two to four people doesn't fit a tall frame. Follow Speaker solves that: in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), it reads each person's microphone and cuts the frame to whoever is talking.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
13	  where="Follow ▸ Speaker in the sheet"
14	  tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']}
15	  needs="A microphone for each person, on its own track. Faces are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## What you need
19	
20	- A wide shot: a full-frame movie clip with the people in it.
21	- A sound file for each person, from a recorder or a lavalier rather than a camera, each on its own track and recorded with the shot.
22	- Those sound files lined up with the shot. Use [**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**](/audio/synchronize-audio/) first.
23	
24	## Follow the speaker
25	
26	<Steps>
27	
28	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** and set **Follow** to **Speaker**. The **Microphones** and **Faces** rows appear.
29	
30	2. Under [**Microphones**](#microphones), tick the tracks that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.
31	
32	3. Under [**Faces**](#faces), check that each row names that microphone's person. If the movies haven't been analysed yet the pop-ups have no faces for now.
33	
34	4. Choose **Make**. If an analysis has to run first, [the sheet comes back](#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis) when it's done, so you can do step 3 and choose **Make** there.
35	
36	</Steps>
37	
38	The other controls work as they do in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/#the-controls).
39	
40	## Microphones
41	
42	A checkbox for each track holding a sound file, named by the track and listed front to back. A camera's track isn't offered, and neither is one whose clips all have their sound off. The first four are ticked.
43	
44	Tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot.
45	
46	When no full-frame movie plays beside two ticked microphones, the sheet says "No full-frame movie clip plays beside two of the ticked microphones, so nobody can be framed by who is talking." and **Make** stays off.
47	
48	## Faces
49	
50	One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way. Faces are numbered left to right, with where each sits across the picture: **Face 1 (42 % across)**.
51	
52	Ticking or unticking a microphone rebuilds the rows and offers the match again for the new set. Otherwise your own choice stands.
53	
54	### The automatic match
55	
56	Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. When the match is clear the pop-ups are already set, and the note under them reads "Each microphone is matched to the face that talks with it; change one if it is wrong." Check that each row names that microphone's person.
57	
58	A match is clear when every microphone agrees with its face to at least 0.2, on a scale where 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is none. A face is counted when it's in at least a quarter of the shot, and four faces at most are considered.
59	
60	### Choose a face
61	
62	When the match isn't clear, each pop-up says **Choose a face** and the note reads "The faces do not show clearly who is on each microphone: choose each microphone's face." Pick each microphone's face yourself.
63	
64	If the shot shows fewer faces than the ticked microphones under it, the pop-ups have no faces to offer. Untick the microphones of people who aren't in it.
65	
66	## When Make is offered
67	
68	**Make** is on when all of these are true:
69	
70	- Two to four microphones are ticked.
71	- A shot plays beside two of them.
72	- Every ticked microphone has a face of its own. Two microphones can't share a face.
73	
74	While an analysis is still to be made there are no faces to choose yet, so the last rule waits: **Make** is on with the first two, and pressing it runs the analysis.
75	
76	A microphone imported moments ago may still be being measured. The sheet says so in the words [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) uses, such as "The microphone on track 3 is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet. Try again in a moment." Choose the command again in a moment. A microphone with no speech under the shot stops **Make** in the same way, with "The microphone on track 3 has no speech between …". Untick it.
77	
78	## The sheet comes back after analysis
79	
80	The summary warns you first: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then asks you to confirm who is on each microphone, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
81	
82	When you choose **Make**, the Analyzing sheet runs. Then the sheet comes back on the same shape, **Follow**, **Zoom**, **Where Empty**, **Make a copy** and ticked microphones, this time with faces to confirm. Nothing is made until you choose **Make** there. **Stop** on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.
83	
84	## How the shot is cut
85	
86	A shot is framed this way when it's a full-frame movie, its file is present, it has no cursor file, it isn't on a microphone track, and it overlaps sound on at least two ticked microphones. Frame Job doesn't count the people in it. The summary counts these shots: "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip."
87	
88	Who talks when is read the way Switch by Speaker reads the microphones, with its default settings, so the two agree.
89	
90	- Each change of speaker is a cut, not a move.
91	- Each framing holds at least 2 s, so a short reply doesn't cut away and back.
92	- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. When they don't, the frame stays on the person already in it.
93	- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.
94	
95	Every other movie clip follows its faces, and screen recordings and everything else are treated as usual. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
96	
97	## Shots that follow their faces instead
98	
99	A shot that can't be framed by who is talking follows its faces instead, and the summary says why: "Clip 3 is followed, but it follows its faces, not who is talking, because …". The reasons include:
100	
101	- It changes shot. Follow Speaker frames one wide shot, so split the clip first with **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**.
102	- It shows fewer faces than the microphones under it.
103	- Nobody talks inside it on those microphones.
104	
105	## Good to know
106	
107	- The faces you confirm come from the longest shot and apply to every shot by number, counting left to right. If people sit in a different order in another shot, that shot frames the wrong person.
108	- A shot uses only the ticked microphones that sound under it, so a microphone used elsewhere in the timeline doesn't count against it.
109	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) doesn't offer **Speaker**. Only Make Vertical Version and an agent do.
110	
111	## With an agent
112	
113	An agent makes the same version with `make_vertical_version`, naming two to four microphone clips, each standing for its track, and the faces if it wants to set them. Nobody confirms a match, so a shot whose faces don't show who is whose follows its faces, with the reason in the answer, unless the call names them. `reframe_clip` frames one clip on whoever is talking, on the canvas it's already on. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
114	
115	## Related
116	
117	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
118	- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
119	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
120	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)

18	| A [blurred copy](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) behind a clip | Removed, or re-filled to cover the new canvas |
19	| A [background plate](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) | Re-filled to cover the new canvas |
20	| A [graphic exactly the old canvas's size](#graphics) | Re-sized to the new canvas |
21	| A [camera or a screen in a camera layout](#camera-layouts) | Laid out again for the new canvas |
22	| A [screen recording with its cursor file](#screen-recordings) that fills the frame | Follows the pointer |
23	| A [movie](#full-frame-movies) that fills the frame | Follows its subject |
24	| A [still, picture or nest](#stills-pictures-and-nests) that fills the frame | Centred |
25	| [Word captions](#word-captions) | Paged again for the narrow frame |
26	| [Everything else](#everything-else) | Kept as placed |
27	
28	A clip **fills the old frame** when its rectangle at its first frame covers the canvas on one side, to within a pixel at each edge, and on the other side is centred to within 2 % or covers that too. So the usual full-frame shot counts, and so does one punched in a little. A picture-in-picture doesn't.
29	
30	A sound-only clip, a clip with its video turned off and an adjustment clip have no picture here, so nothing happens to them.
31	
32	## Full-frame movies
33	
34	A movie clip that fills the old frame follows what you chose in **Follow**, as [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) frames it. Its own moves and actions stay, inside the framing.
35	
36	Where the frame shows the whole picture, a blurred copy of the clip goes behind it, so the canvas around it isn't empty. The copies go on a new **Backgrounds** track at the back, and copies that overlap in time go on further tracks behind it. The track is removed when no copy needs it.
37	
38	The summary tells you how each one went:
39	
40	| The clip | The summary says |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| Follows its subject | It's counted in "Follows 3 clips." |
43	| Has nothing to follow at any point | It's counted in "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." |
44	| Has nothing to follow for part of its length | It's still counted as followed, with "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found." |
45	| Moves by a motion of its own | "Clip 2 is followed, but moves by its own motion: …", with the motion's name, because that move isn't part of the framing. |
46	
47	Some movies can't be followed and are kept as placed, each listed with the reason:
48	
49	- A movie whose file is missing: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." With **Follow** on **Center** it's centred like any other clip instead.
50	- A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or one a matte cuts, because framing would move it out of the matte.
51	- A clip turned by its rotation or by an action, or one that spins in its motion, because framing works on an upright picture.
52	
53	With **Follow** on **Speaker**, a wide shot beside its microphones cuts to whoever is talking, and every other movie follows its faces. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
54	
55	## Screen recordings
56	
57	A screen recording with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) follows the pointer instead of a face, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at.
58	
59	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when it strays from the middle of the frame, by more than 20 % of the frame's width or 12 % of its height.
60	- It arrives on a click outside that area. The move ends on the click's frame, so the click lands in view.
61	- It holds still while you type.
62	- Any zoom and pan of the clip's own, such as [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)'s, is replaced, since the tall frame is already a close-up. The summary says so: "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced."
63	
64	**Where Empty** doesn't apply to a recording that follows its pointer. **Center** centres the recording as any other movie.
65	
66	When the cursor file can't be read, because it was moved or deleted, the recording is shown whole on a blurred copy and the summary says "its cursor file could not be read, so it is shown whole".
67	
68	## Camera layouts
69	
70	A screen recording and its camera in [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) keep their arrangement. This covers the layouts of **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** and the layout a recording landed in. Each switch is made again for the new canvas, at the same time, length and curve.
71	
72	| On the old canvas | On the new canvas |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| A Corner | A Corner in the same corner |
75	| Camera Full | Camera Full |
76	| Side by Side, going to a tall canvas | Stacked, with the screen across the top and the camera below it, so the screen isn't squeezed into two-thirds of a narrow frame |
77	| Side by Side, going to a square | Side by Side |
78	
79	The camera, the screen and the cut pieces of either are never followed and get no blurred copy. A zoom on the screen keeps showing the same part of the picture.
80	
81	The summary counts them, "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas.", and lists each switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
82	
83	A circle or panel crop is re-centred on the middle of the crop it had. A crop that had room to move may sit nearer the middle of the camera picture than a switch made directly on the new canvas would.
84	
85	### A layout changed by hand
86	
87	If a camera was moved or resized by more than a pixel after its switch, it's no longer a layout Frame Job made. The camera and its screen are kept as placed, and the summary says "Clip 6 is not followed: its camera layout was edited by hand, so it is kept as placed."
88	
89	## Stills, pictures and nests
90	
91	A still or a picture that fills the frame is centred, and so is a [nest](/editing/nests/) that does. There's nothing inside them to follow. The summary lists each one: "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a still picture, so it is centred." or "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a nest, so it is centred."
92	
93	What's inside a nest isn't reframed. A still, picture or nest that doesn't fill the frame is [kept as placed](#everything-else).
94	
95	## Graphics
96	
97	A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, such as a full-frame lower third or title card, is re-sized to the new canvas, so it lays itself out again on the narrow frame. Its position and the positions its actions move it to shrink and stretch with the two sides, and its scale stays as it was. Any other graphic is [kept as placed](#everything-else).
98	
99	Older copies of the bundled templates in the project are updated in a copy, and listed when you apply the step in place: "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height is listed too, and never rewritten. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
100	
101	## Everything else
102	
103	Titles, other graphics, shapes, a picture-in-picture and any clip that doesn't fill the frame are kept as placed. They're moved and scaled from the old canvas to the new one, as the Document tab does when a [canvas change](/projects/canvas-size/) rescales clips:
104	
105	- A clip's horizontal position follows the change in width.
106	- Its vertical position follows the change in height.
107	- Its scale follows the smaller of the two changes, so something that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one.
108	
109	From 1920 × 1080 to 1080 × 1920, a title's distance from the centre shrinks to 0.56 across and grows to 1.78 down, and the title itself shrinks to 0.56 of its size. The positions and scales its actions move to change the same way.
110	
111	## Blurred copies and background plates
112	
113	A blurred copy already behind a clip is removed when that clip is framed, because the framing makes a new one where it's needed. Otherwise it's re-filled to cover the new canvas. A copy counts as one when it's named **Blurred Background** and a clip of the same source, start and length sits in front of it.
114	
115	A background plate from **Clip ▸ Add Background** is re-filled too. A plate is a rectangle shape the canvas's size, centred at scale 1, or an image or still named **Background** that fills the canvas. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
116	
117	## Word captions
118	
119	Word captions are paged again for the narrow frame from the words their pages hold, every correction kept, as **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** does. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/). A track that was hidden or locked stays that way.
120	
121	A caption track that can't be re-laid is kept as placed, and the summary names it: "Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings." That happens to [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/), and to a track when:
122	
123	- it's a matte track
124	- a page has no word timings, or none of a page's words starts inside it
125	- a page is in a style Frame Job doesn't make, or its pages are in more than one style
126	- its pages wouldn't fit
127	
128	## Related

1	---
2	title: Follow the speaker in a vertical
3	description: Make a vertical version of a wide interview that cuts to whoever is talking, using a microphone per person.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A wide shot of two to four people doesn't fit a tall frame. Follow Speaker solves that: in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), it reads each person's microphone and cuts the frame to whoever is talking.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
13	  where="Follow ▸ Speaker in the sheet"
14	  tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']}
15	  needs="A microphone for each person, on its own track. Faces are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## What you need
19	
20	- A wide shot: a full-frame movie clip with the people in it.
21	- A sound file for each person, from a recorder or a lavalier rather than a camera, each on its own track and recorded with the shot.
22	- Those sound files lined up with the shot. Use [**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**](/audio/synchronize-audio/) first.
23	
24	## Follow the speaker
25	
26	<Steps>
27	
28	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** and set **Follow** to **Speaker**. The **Microphones** and **Faces** rows appear.
29	
30	2. Under [**Microphones**](#microphones), tick the tracks that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.
31	
32	3. Under [**Faces**](#faces), check that each row names that microphone's person. If the movies haven't been analysed yet the pop-ups have no faces for now.
33	
34	4. Choose **Make**. If an analysis has to run first, [the sheet comes back](#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis) when it's done, so you can do step 3 and choose **Make** there.
35	
36	</Steps>
37	
38	The other controls work as they do in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/#the-controls).
39	
40	## Microphones
41	
42	A checkbox for each track holding a sound file, named by the track and listed front to back. A camera's track isn't offered, and neither is one whose clips all have their sound off. The first four are ticked.
43	
44	Tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot.
45	
46	When no full-frame movie plays beside two ticked microphones, the sheet says "No full-frame movie clip plays beside two of the ticked microphones, so nobody can be framed by who is talking." and **Make** stays off.
47	
48	## Faces
49	
50	One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way. Faces are numbered left to right, with where each sits across the picture: **Face 1 (42 % across)**.
51	
52	Ticking or unticking a microphone rebuilds the rows and offers the match again for the new set. Otherwise your own choice stands.
53	
54	### The automatic match
55	
56	Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. When the match is clear the pop-ups are already set, and the note under them reads "Each microphone is matched to the face that talks with it; change one if it is wrong." Check that each row names that microphone's person.
57	
58	A match is clear when every microphone agrees with its face to at least 0.2, on a scale where 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is none. A face is counted when it's in at least a quarter of the shot, and four faces at most are considered.
59	
60	### Choose a face
61	
62	When the match isn't clear, each pop-up says **Choose a face** and the note reads "The faces do not show clearly who is on each microphone: choose each microphone's face." Pick each microphone's face yourself.
63	
64	If the shot shows fewer faces than the ticked microphones under it, the pop-ups have no faces to offer. Untick the microphones of people who aren't in it.
65	
66	## When Make is offered
67	
68	**Make** is on when all of these are true:
69	
70	- Two to four microphones are ticked.
71	- A shot plays beside two of them.
72	- Every ticked microphone has a face of its own. Two microphones can't share a face.
73	
74	While an analysis is still to be made there are no faces to choose yet, so the last rule waits: **Make** is on with the first two, and pressing it runs the analysis.
75	
76	A microphone imported moments ago may still be being measured. The sheet says so in the words [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) uses, such as "The microphone on track 3 is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet. Try again in a moment." Choose the command again in a moment. A microphone with no speech under the shot stops **Make** in the same way, with "The microphone on track 3 has no speech between …". Untick it.
77	
78	## The sheet comes back after analysis
79	
80	The summary warns you first: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then asks you to confirm who is on each microphone, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
81	
82	When you choose **Make**, the Analyzing sheet runs. Then the sheet comes back on the same shape, **Follow**, **Zoom**, **Where Empty**, **Make a copy** and ticked microphones, this time with faces to confirm. Nothing is made until you choose **Make** there. **Stop** on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.
83	
84	## How the shot is cut
85	
86	A shot is framed this way when it's a full-frame movie, its file is present, it has no cursor file, it isn't on a microphone track, and it overlaps sound on at least two ticked microphones. Frame Job doesn't count the people in it. The summary counts these shots: "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip."
87	
88	Who talks when is read the way Switch by Speaker reads the microphones, with its default settings, so the two agree.
89	
90	- Each change of speaker is a cut, not a move.
91	- Each framing holds at least 2 s, so a short reply doesn't cut away and back.
92	- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. When they don't, the frame stays on the person already in it.
93	- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.
94	
95	Every other movie clip follows its faces, and screen recordings and everything else are treated as usual. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
96	
97	## Shots that follow their faces instead
98	
99	A shot that can't be framed by who is talking follows its faces instead, and the summary says why: "Clip 3 is followed, but it follows its faces, not who is talking, because …". The reasons include:
100	
101	- It changes shot. Follow Speaker frames one wide shot, so split the clip first with **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**.
102	- It shows fewer faces than the microphones under it.
103	- Nobody talks inside it on those microphones.
104	
105	## Good to know
106	
107	- The faces you confirm come from the longest shot and apply to every shot by number, counting left to right. If people sit in a different order in another shot, that shot frames the wrong person.
108	- A shot uses only the ticked microphones that sound under it, so a microphone used elsewhere in the timeline doesn't count against it.
109	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) doesn't offer **Speaker**. Only Make Vertical Version and an agent do.
110	
111	## With an agent
112	
113	An agent makes the same version with `make_vertical_version`, naming two to four microphone clips, each standing for its track, and the faces if it wants to set them. Nobody confirms a match, so a shot whose faces don't show who is whose follows its faces, with the reason in the answer, unless the call names them. `reframe_clip` frames one clip on whoever is talking, on the canvas it's already on. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
114	
115	## Related
116	
117	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
118	- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
119	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
120	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)

44:| `speaker` | Cuts to whoever is talking in a wide shot | Yes, and the microphones' speech |

50:The first four rows move the frame over time. The sheets don't offer all of these. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** has Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region and Center, **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** adds Speaker, and Make Vertical uses `cursor`, `fit`, `layout` and `keep` by itself where a clip calls for them. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
60:A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use `subject` or these three, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces.
62:### `cursor`
64:Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). A screen recording made by Frame Job has one.
72:If the cursor file is missing or won't open, the agent is told which file and why. The **Cursor** section of the Media tab has **Locate…** to point the media at a moved file.
74:### `speaker`
78:- **Who talks when** is read from the microphones exactly as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads them with its default settings, so the two agree.
80:- **Each change of speaker** is a cut, held at least 2 s.
82:- **While nobody talks**, the last speaker stays.
    static func offered(_ canvas: CanvasSnapshot) -> [VerticalShape] {
        VerticalShape.allCases.filter { shape in
            let size = shape.size(from: canvas)
            return size.width != canvas.width || size.height != canvas.height
        }
    }

    /// "moves by its own motion: <name>" for the first active slot that is neither a fade nor
    /// a spin, in the order during, in, out; nil when there is none.
    static func motionNote(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> String? {
        guard let motion = clip.videoProps.motion else { return nil }
        if let during = motion.during, during.amount > 0, during.kind != .spin {
            return "moves by its own motion: \(during.kind.displayName)"
        }
        for edge in [motion.inEdge, motion.out].compactMap({ $0 })
        where edge.isActive && edge.kind != .fade && edge.kind != .spin {
            return "moves by its own motion: \(edge.kind.displayName)"
        }
        return nil
    }

## With an agent

`make_vertical_version` tells the agent how each clip was treated and why, which clips followed their pointer, and each layout switch it made again. It can also leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again. `reframe_clip` applies one of these framings to a single clip. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
